quote: | REQ-4 | An empty cart cannot be checked out. |
title: REQ-4 (empty cart cannot be checked out) is implemented nowhere; its test asserts the opposite-looking behaviour
evidence: src/cart.py has only total() and discounted(); no checkout function, no guard, no exception. tests/test_cart.py:16-17 is tagged REQ-4 but asserts total([]) == 0, which treats an empty cart as a valid cart with total 0. Traced; total([]) returned 0 when run.
failing_case: A caller checks out [] : total([]) returns 0 and nothing refuses it, so a zero-value order goes through. The suite is green, so the missing rule is reported as covered.
remediation: Add a checkout or validate function that raises on an empty cart, and change the REQ-4 test to assert that refusal (pytest.raises). Keep total([]) == 0 as a separate arithmetic test.

title: REQ-4 (empty cart cannot be checked out) is implemented nowhere
evidence: docs/requirements.md:9 states REQ-4. src/cart.py holds only total() and discounted(); there is no checkout function, no guard, no raise for an empty list. total([]) returns sum([]) == 0 and nothing refuses it.
failing_case: A caller passes an empty cart: total([]) returns 0 and discounted(0, 10) returns 0.0. Nothing in the module signals 'cannot check out', so a zero-value order goes through.
remediation: Add a checkout/validate function that raises (or returns an explicit error) for an empty cart, and test that it refuses; keep total() pure.

title: test_empty_checkout claims REQ-4 but asserts the opposite behaviour of the requirement
evidence: The body is `assert total([]) == 0`. REQ-4 says an empty cart cannot be checked out; the test only pins that the sum of nothing is 0. No checkout is called and no refusal is asserted. Because the citation comment marks REQ-4 as covered, the gap in src/cart.py (no guard) is hidden.
failing_case: Implement REQ-4 by making total([]) raise, and this test fails; leave REQ-4 unimplemented and it passes. It protects the wrong behaviour.
remediation: Replace with a test that calls the checkout function with [] and asserts it raises or returns the refusal; remove the REQ-4 tag from the total() assertion.

title: REQ-2 test only covers the floor; the percentage reduction is untested and negative percentages raise the price
evidence: Mutation run in-process: replacing discounted with `lambda a, p: 0` still passes test_discount_floor. No test checks a normal discount such as discounted(100, 10) == 90. In src/cart.py:6 percent is not validated.
failing_case: A change that returns 0 for every code (or ignores percent) passes the suite while every customer gets a free cart. Separately, discounted(100, -50) returns 150.0: a negative-percent code increases the total, contradicting 'reduces the total'.
remediation: Add tests for a normal percentage (discounted(100, 10) == 90) and for 0 and 100 percent. Reject percent outside 0..100 in discounted() and test the rejection.

title: REQ-3 test formats the value itself, so it tests Python's f-string and not the code; the code returns unrounded floats
evidence: The test applies :.2f in the test body; nothing in src/cart.py does any formatting or rounding. total([0.1, 0.2]) returns 0.30000000000000004 (run). The test passes whatever total or any display code does.
failing_case: Any display code that prints total() directly shows 0.30000000000000004 and the suite stays green. Money is also summed as binary floats, so totals drift (0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3).
remediation: Add a named display function (format_price) in src/cart.py, test that, and compute money with Decimal or integer cents.
